pharm: Prodrug of thiorphan, an inhibitor of intestinal enkephalinase (neutral endopeptidase); reduces intestinal hypersecretion of water and electrolytes without affecting gut transit
quick: 100 mg three times daily before main meals
Take before meals (adults); children with food
Caution; limited data, no specific adjustment established

summary: Racecadotril is an orally active prodrug of thiorphan that inhibits intestinal enkephalinase (neutral endopeptidase), protecting endogenous enkephalins and thereby reducing the hypersecretion of water and electrolytes into the intestinal lumen. It is used as an adjunct to oral (or intravenous) rehydration in the symptomatic treatment of acute diarrhoea in adults and children when rehydration alone is insufficient. Unlike loperamide it has a purely antisecretory action and does not slow intestinal transit, so it does not cause constipation or rebound and does not promote bacterial stasis. It is given three times daily before the main meals in adults and as weight-based sachets in children, alongside oral rehydration solution. It is not approved by the FDA and is used mainly in the EU and India.
indications: Symptomatic treatment of acute diarrhoea in adults, as an adjunct to oral rehydration and general supportive measures, when these are insufficient to control symptoms
Symptomatic treatment of acute diarrhoea in infants (older than 3 months) and children, in addition to oral rehydration and supportive measures, when rehydration alone is insufficient

dosage.t: Take before the three main meals; first dose can be taken at any time of day
dosage.n: Continue until two normal stools, max ~7 days; if no improvement in 48 h reassess and consider alternative

dosage.c: Acute diarrhoea (infant >3 months / children, by weight)
dosage.d: 1.5 mg/kg per dose three times daily (e.g. <9 kg: 10 mg TID; 9-13 kg: 20 mg TID; 13-27 kg: 30 mg TID; >27 kg: 60 mg TID)
dosage.t: Three times daily, with food, alongside oral rehydration solution
dosage.n: Maximum 7 days; if diarrhoea persists or worsens, reassess for dehydration and other causes

admin: Always give with adequate oral (or, if needed, intravenous) rehydration and dietary measures - racecadotril is an adjunct, not a replacement for rehydration
Adults: take 100 mg capsules before the main meals; the first dose may be taken at any time of day
Children: disperse the appropriate weight-based sachet of granules in food, water or infant feed and give immediately, with meals
Treat only acute diarrhoea; do not use for chronic diarrhoea or beyond the recommended short course (about 7 days)
Seek medical advice if there is high fever, blood or pus in the stools, or signs of significant dehydration
moa: Racecadotril is a prodrug that is rapidly hydrolysed to its active metabolite thiorphan, a selective and reversible inhibitor of enkephalinase (neutral endopeptidase, a cell-membrane peptidase). By inhibiting the breakdown of endogenous enkephalins at the intestinal mucosa, it prolongs their antisecretory action on enterocyte delta-opioid receptors. This reduces cyclic-AMP-mediated hypersecretion of water and electrolytes into the intestinal lumen, without altering basal secretory activity. Racecadotril acts only on intestinal secretion and does not affect intestinal transit time, so it relieves diarrhoea without causing constipation. It does not have central effects at therapeutic doses.

Children under 3 months of age (insufficient data)
Conditions where it cannot be combined with adequate rehydration
relative: Diabetes or galactose intolerance/glucose-galactose malabsorption (sucrose/lactose-containing sachets)
Diarrhoea with high fever, blood or mucus suggesting invasive bacterial infection

Persistence beyond the recommended treatment duration

preg: There are insufficient data on the use of racecadotril in pregnant women. As a precaution, it is not recommended during pregnancy and should be avoided unless the potential benefit clearly outweighs the risk.
lact: Because of a lack of information on excretion in human milk, racecadotril should not be used in women who are breastfeeding.
renal: Data in patients with renal impairment are limited; use with caution. No specific dose adjustment has been established, and the short duration of treatment for acute diarrhoea limits exposure.
hepatic: Data in patients with hepatic impairment are limited; use with caution. No specific dose adjustment has been established for short-term treatment of acute diarrhoea.

major: ACE inhibitors (e.g. captopril, enalapril, lisinopril) - concomitant enkephalinase/neprilysin-type inhibition has been associated with an increased risk of angioedema; use with caution
moderate: Other neprilysin inhibitors (e.g. sacubitril) - theoretical additive risk of angioedema
Drugs that themselves cause angioedema - additive risk
minor: No clinically significant pharmacokinetic interactions established at therapeutic doses
interactions.food: Adults take doses before main meals; children take with food. Food does not markedly impair efficacy. Always combine with oral rehydration solution.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction reported; alcohol is best avoided during an episode of acute diarrhoea.
interactions.diagnostics: No clinically significant interference with laboratory tests established.

serious: Angioedema (face, lips, tongue, larynx) - rare but potentially serious, sometimes after the first dose

monitoring: Hydration status and need for continued oral/IV rehydration
Stool frequency and clinical response within 48 hours
Signs of hypersensitivity or angioedema, especially after the first dose
Re-evaluation if diarrhoea persists, recurs, or is accompanied by fever, blood, or vomiting
Limiting treatment to the recommended short course (about 7 days)
counsel: This medicine controls the watery secretion of diarrhoea but is not a substitute for drinking plenty of rehydration fluids
Keep taking oral rehydration solution and fluids to replace what is lost
Adults: take the capsule before your main meals; for children, mix the sachet in food or drink and give immediately
Stop and seek medical advice if you develop swelling of the face, lips or tongue, difficulty breathing, or a rash
Seek medical advice if diarrhoea lasts more than 2 days, or if there is high fever, blood in the stool, or signs of dehydration (very dry mouth, little urine, drowsiness)
Unlike some antidiarrheals it does not slow the gut or cause constipation
pk: Antidiarrheal effect within about 1 hour of an oral dose
Active metabolite (thiorphan) plasma peak at approximately 1 hour; antisecretory effect peaks around 2 hours
Plasma elimination half-life of the active metabolite approximately 3 hours
Effect lasts about 8 hours, supporting three-times-daily dosing
Store below 30°C; keep capsules/sachets in original packaging, protected from moisture
pearls: Not FDA-approved in the US; it is used in the EU and India for acute diarrhoea and the doses here are sourced from the SmPC/BNF, not an FDA label
Acts only as an intestinal antisecretory agent - it does not slow gut transit, so it does not cause constipation or rebound and does not favour bacterial overgrowth (a key contrast with loperamide)
Always an adjunct to oral rehydration, not a replacement - rehydration remains the cornerstone of acute diarrhoea management, especially in children
Concomitant ACE inhibitors increase the risk of angioedema - counsel patients to stop and seek care if facial/tongue swelling occurs
If diarrhoea does not improve within 48 hours, reassess for invasive infection or another cause rather than continuing
Paediatric sachets are dosed by body weight (about 1.5 mg/kg three times daily) and given with feeds
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered before continuing the usual three-times-daily schedule; if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one and do not double up. Treatment is short term, so simply resume normal dosing and keep up rehydration fluids.
overdose: Experience with overdose is limited. Doses well above the therapeutic range have generally been well tolerated. Management is symptomatic and supportive, with attention to fluid and electrolyte balance; there is no specific antidote. Monitor for hypersensitivity reactions.
